t: Section 44303 of title 49, United States Code, is amended in paragraph (b) by deleting “December 31, 2013” and inserting “the date specified in section 106(3) of the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2014” in lieu thereof.

fable.w: This section only changes an expiration date in 49 U.S.C. 44303 by substituting a cross-reference to the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2014. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. There is no real tempting reading here, since no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended in paragraph (b) by deleting “December 31, 2013” and inserting “the date specified in section 106(3) of the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2014” in lieu thereof.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute that changes a specific date. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative housekeeping provision.
qwen_block.s: Section 44303 of title 49, United States Code, is amended in paragraph (b) by deleting “December 31, 2013” and inserting “the date specified in section 106(3) of the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2014” in lieu thereof.

opus.w: This section only changes a date in 49 U.S.C. 44303(b), replacing "December 31, 2013" with a date tied to the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2014. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory committee or right to sue. No outside party takes part in a federal decision. The fact that it amends a statute that may affect private carriers is not enough to count as participation.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** Someone might read this as participation because it amends a federal aviation statute (49 U.S.C. 44303, on aviation insurance coverage), which could involve outside parties such as air carriers. That reading fails. The amendment only swaps one date for another. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
